transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in today because... well, I keep hearing Garrett's voice. It's as clear as if he's standing right behind me when I'm out on the trail or in my painting room. And, you know, even though part of me knows he's dead... in the moment, it feels completely real. It's been really intense, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been hearing Garrett's voice?
It's been about a month. Basically, this whole crisis has been unfolding ever since he died... so, yeah, roughly four weeks now.
Have you been feeling unusually depressed, hopeless, or perhaps the opposite, like you have an extreme amount of energy and aren't needing much sleep?

I haven't really felt depressed, no. It's been more of the opposite. 

At first, I felt almost... lit up, I guess. Like I had this urgent purpose that no one else could see. But it wasn't just having energy. I would actually snap into a rage if anyone questioned me about what I was doing, or, you know, if they tried to slow me down.
When you are in these states of high energy and rage, do you find that your thoughts are racing, or that it is difficult to keep your conversation on track?

Yeah, they definitely race. It's like they move so fast I can't even keep up with them. I'll have just one simple idea about a patient note for work, and suddenly that turns into five different projects... and then my mind just jumps to a memory from a hike, and then straight into guilt about the funeral. All of that happens before I can even catch a single thought. So, yeah, it gets pretty difficult to stay on track.
Over the past four weeks, have these periods of high energy and racing thoughts been constant, or do they come and go in shorter bursts?

It's pretty much been constant. Um, ever since Garrett passed, I haven't really had a break from it. The racing thoughts, the energy, the anger... it's just been going on this whole time, day in and day out. I haven't felt it stop or even slow down.
Are there any times during these past four weeks where you have heard Garrett's voice when you were not feeling that high energy or racing thoughts?

No, I haven't. I only started hearing his voice during this... this wired stretch, where I'm barely sleeping and taking on all these impossible projects. It's like I'm just driven to keep going. I never heard him like that before this whole mood shift happened. It wasn't something that was happening during just... ordinary grief, you know? It only started with the energy.
